Chapter 26 — Inverse Trigonometric Functions

Kanna, ordinary sine takes an angle and gives a number. Inverse sine takes a number and returns one chosen angle. “One chosen angle” is the main idea in this chapter.

Your preparation target remains 200 marks: Physics 60, Maths 60, Chemistry 80. Train yourself to check three things: the input is allowed,the returned angle is in its principal range,and any transformed equation still satisfies the original.

Concept C01 — Why an inverse needs a chosen branch

sin⁡(π/6)=sin⁡(5π/6)=1/2\sin(\pi/6)=\sin(5\pi/6)=1/2sin(π/6)=sin(5π/6)=1/2. If we ask “Which angle has sine 1/21/21/2?”,there are many answers. A function must return one output for each input.

We therefore restrict ordinary sine to [−π/2,π/2][-\pi/2,\pi/2][−π/2,π/2],where it increases without repeating. The inverse of this restricted function is inverse sine,also written arcsin⁡\arcsinarcsin:

y=sin⁡−1u  ⟺  sin⁡y=u,−π/2≤y≤π/2.\boxed{y=\sin^{-1}u \iff \sin y=u,\quad -\pi/2\le y\le\pi/2}.y=sin−1u⟺siny=u,−π/2≤y≤π/2​.

The chosen output interval is its principal range. “Principal” means the standard chosen branch.

Very important notation:

sin⁡−1u=arcsin⁡ubut1sin⁡u=csc⁡u.\sin^{-1}u=\arcsin u \quad\text{but}\quad \frac1{\sin u}=\csc u.sin−1u=arcsinubutsinu1​=cscu.

The superscript −1-1−1 here means inverse function,not reciprocal. Inverse sine returns an angle; reciprocal sine returns a number obtained by division.

Undoing works in two different ways:

sin⁡(sin⁡−1u)=u(−1≤u≤1),\boxed{\sin(\sin^{-1}u)=u\quad(-1\le u\le1)},sin(sin−1u)=u(−1≤u≤1)​,

but

sin⁡−1(sin⁡x)=x only when −π/2≤x≤π/2.\boxed{\sin^{-1}(\sin x)=x \text{ only when }-\pi/2\le x\le\pi/2}.sin−1(sinx)=x only when −π/2≤x≤π/2​.

Outside that interval,find the equivalent principal angle. Do not cancel the symbols as if both formulas held for every real input.

Concept C02 — Inverse sine and inverse cosine

arcsin⁡:[−1,1]⟶[−π/2,π/2],\boxed{\arcsin:[-1,1]\longrightarrow[-\pi/2,\pi/2]},arcsin:[−1,1]⟶[−π/2,π/2]​, arccos⁡:[−1,1]⟶[0,π].\boxed{\arccos:[-1,1]\longrightarrow[0,\pi]}.arccos:[−1,1]⟶[0,π]​.

Both accept numbers only between −1-1−1 and 1. Their output intervals differ.

Read the axes: the horizontal input is a sine/cosine value. The vertical output is an angle in radians. Arcsine increases; arccosine decreases.

Input uuu −1-1−1 −1/2-1/2−1/2 000 1/21/21/2 111
arcsin⁡u\arcsin uarcsinu −π/2-\pi/2−π/2 −π/6-\pi/6−π/6 000 π/6\pi/6π/6 π/2\pi/2π/2
arccos⁡u\arccos uarccosu π\piπ 2π/32\pi/32π/3 π/2\pi/2π/2 π/3\pi/3π/3 000

For u∈[−1,1]u\in[-1,1]u∈[−1,1],

arcsin⁡u+arccos⁡u=π/2,\boxed{\arcsin u+\arccos u=\pi/2},arcsinu+arccosu=π/2​, arcsin⁡(−u)=−arcsin⁡u,arccos⁡(−u)=π−arccos⁡u.\arcsin(-u)=-\arcsin u,\qquad \arccos(-u)=\pi-\arccos u.arcsin(−u)=−arcsinu,arccos(−u)=π−arccosu.

Why complementary? If A=arcsin⁡uA=\arcsin uA=arcsinu,then cos⁡(π/2−A)=u\cos(\pi/2-A)=ucos(π/2−A)=u,and π/2−A\pi/2-Aπ/2−A is in [0,π][0,\pi][0,π]. It is exactly the arccosine output.

arctan⁡u+arccot⁡u=π/2,\boxed{\arctan u+\operatorname{arccot}u=\pi/2},arctanu+arccotu=π/2​, arctan⁡(−u)=−arctan⁡u,arccot⁡(−u)=π−arccot⁡u.\arctan(-u)=-\arctan u,\qquad \operatorname{arccot}(-u)=\pi-\operatorname{arccot}u.arctan(−u)=−arctanu,arccot(−u)=π−arccotu.

arccot⁡u={arctan⁡(1/u),u>0,π/2,u=0,π+arctan⁡(1/u),u<0.\operatorname{arccot}u= \begin{cases} \arctan(1/u),&u>0,\\ \pi/2,&u=0,\\ \pi+\arctan(1/u),&u<0. \end{cases}arccotu=⎩⎨⎧​arctan(1/u),π/2,π+arctan(1/u),​u>0,u=0,u<0.​

Concept C04 — Folding an angle into its principal range

To evaluate arcsin⁡(sin⁡x)\arcsin(\sin x)arcsin(sinx),find an angle with the same sine inside [−π/2,π/2][-\pi/2,\pi/2][−π/2,π/2].

For integer nnn and x∈[nπ−π/2,nπ+π/2]x\in[n\pi-\pi/2,n\pi+\pi/2]x∈[nπ−π/2,nπ+π/2],

arcsin⁡(sin⁡x)=(−1)n(x−nπ).\boxed{\arcsin(\sin x)=(-1)^n(x-n\pi)}.arcsin(sinx)=(−1)n(x−nπ)​.

Do not memorize this before understanding the fold. Examples:

arcsin⁡(sin⁡(3π/4))=π/4,arcsin⁡(sin⁡π)=0.\arcsin(\sin(3\pi/4))=\pi/4,\qquad \arcsin(\sin\pi)=0.arcsin(sin(3π/4))=π/4,arcsin(sinπ)=0.

For cosine,first reduce the input to t∈[0,2π)t\in[0,2\pi)t∈[0,2π) by full turns:

arccos⁡(cos⁡x)={t,0≤t≤π,2π−t,π<t<2π.\arccos(\cos x)= \begin{cases} t,&0\le t\le\pi,\\ 2\pi-t,&\pi<t<2\pi. \end{cases}arccos(cosx)={t,2π−t,​0≤t≤π,π<t<2π.​

For tangent,choose the unique integer nnn with

−π/2<x−nπ<π/2.-\pi/2<x-n\pi<\pi/2.−π/2<x−nπ<π/2.

Then arctan⁡(tan⁡x)=x−nπ\arctan(\tan x)=x-n\piarctan(tanx)=x−nπ. At tangent's excluded endpoints,the original inner function is undefined.

Fast habit: write the principal range beside the expression,locate the input on the circle,and reflect/subtract turns until the answer lies in that range.

Concept C05 — Replace inverse symbols by ordinary angle names

If A=arcsin⁡uA=\arcsin uA=arcsinu,then sin⁡A=u\sin A=usinA=u and cos⁡A≥0\cos A\ge0cosA≥0. Thus

cos⁡(arcsin⁡u)=1−u2.\boxed{\cos(\arcsin u)=\sqrt{1-u^2}}.cos(arcsinu)=1−u2​​.

For ∣u∣<1|u|<1∣u∣<1,

tan⁡(arcsin⁡u)=u1−u2.\tan(\arcsin u)=\frac{u}{\sqrt{1-u^2}}.tan(arcsinu)=1−u2​u​.

If B=arccos⁡uB=\arccos uB=arccosu,then sin⁡B≥0\sin B\ge0sinB≥0,so

sin⁡(arccos⁡u)=1−u2.\boxed{\sin(\arccos u)=\sqrt{1-u^2}}.sin(arccosu)=1−u2​​.

Its tangent is 1−u2/u\sqrt{1-u^2}/u1−u2​/u when u≠0u\ne0u=0; it can be negative if BBB is obtuse.

If C=arctan⁡uC=\arctan uC=arctanu,then cos⁡C>0\cos C>0cosC>0:

cos⁡C=11+u2,sin⁡C=u1+u2.\boxed{\cos C=\frac1{\sqrt{1+u^2}}}, \qquad \boxed{\sin C=\frac{u}{\sqrt{1+u^2}}}.cosC=1+u2​1​​,sinC=1+u2​u​​.

Why the square-root sign matters: 1−u2\sqrt{1-u^2}1−u2​ is nonnegative. The principal range tells us whether the needed sine/cosine is nonnegative. A freely chosen nonprincipal angle may require the opposite sign.

For an acute ratio such as cos⁡A=4/5\cos A=4/5cosA=4/5,draw adjacent leg 4,hypotenuse 5,then opposite leg 25−16=3\sqrt{25-16}=325−16​=3. This gives an actual triangle before substitution.

Concept C06 — Arctangent sums: tangent is not the whole angle

Let A=arctan⁡uA=\arctan uA=arctanu, B=arctan⁡vB=\arctan vB=arctanv,and S=A+BS=A+BS=A+B. Each angle lies in (−π/2,π/2)(-\pi/2,\pi/2)(−π/2,π/2),so S∈(−π,π)S\in(-\pi,\pi)S∈(−π,π).

When uv≠1uv\ne1uv=1,

tan⁡S=u+v1−uv.\tan S=\frac{u+v}{1-uv}.tanS=1−uvu+v​.

But taking arctan⁡\arctanarctan of that fraction always returns a principal angle. We may need to restore π\piπ:

arctan⁡u+arctan⁡v={arctan⁡u+v1−uv,uv<1,π+arctan⁡u+v1−uv,uv>1, u,v>0,−π+arctan⁡u+v1−uv,uv>1, u,v<0.\boxed{ \arctan u+\arctan v= \begin{cases} \arctan\frac{u+v}{1-uv},&uv<1,\\ \pi+\arctan\frac{u+v}{1-uv},&uv>1,\ u,v>0,\\ -\pi+\arctan\frac{u+v}{1-uv},&uv>1,\ u,v<0. \end{cases}}arctanu+arctanv=⎩⎨⎧​arctan1−uvu+v​,π+arctan1−uvu+v​,−π+arctan1−uvu+v​,​uv<1,uv>1, u,v>0,uv>1, u,v<0.​​

If uv=1uv=1uv=1,both have the same nonzero sign; the sum is π/2\pi/2π/2 for positive inputs and −π/2-\pi/2−π/2 for negative inputs.

Why the cases occur:

cos⁡S=1−uv(1+u2)(1+v2).\cos S=\frac{1-uv}{\sqrt{(1+u^2)(1+v^2)}}.cosS=(1+u2)(1+v2)​1−uv​.

For uv<1uv<1uv<1,cosine is positive,placing SSS in the principal arctangent interval. For positive u,vu,vu,v with uv>1uv>1uv>1,the sum is in quadrant II.

For example,arctan⁡2+arctan⁡3=3π/4\arctan2+\arctan3=3\pi/4arctan2+arctan3=3π/4,whereas arctan⁡(−1)=−π/4\arctan(-1)=-\pi/4arctan(−1)=−π/4. Same tangent,different angles.

For a difference,write arctan⁡u−arctan⁡v=arctan⁡u+arctan⁡(−v)\arctan u-\arctan v=\arctan u+\arctan(-v)arctanu−arctanv=arctanu+arctan(−v) and use the same sign/range logic. The raw tangent fraction is (u−v)/(1+uv)(u-v)/(1+uv)(u−v)/(1+uv) when its denominator is nonzero.

Concept C07 — Equations: apply a function without forgetting its information loss

If two angles are equal,their sines,cosines and tangents are equal where defined. The reverse implication can fail because those functions repeat.

A safe order for inverse-function equations:

  1. Intersect all original domains.
  2. Give inverse expressions angle names and record their principal ranges.
  3. Apply an identity or ordinary trig function to obtain algebraic candidates.
  4. Check every candidate in the original equation,or prove the branch condition that makes the transformation reversible.

For A=arcsin⁡uA=\arcsin uA=arcsinu, B=arcsin⁡vB=\arcsin vB=arcsinv,

sin⁡(A±B)=u1−v2±v1−u2.\sin(A\pm B) =u\sqrt{1-v^2}\pm v\sqrt{1-u^2}.sin(A±B)=u1−v2​±v1−u2​.

Do not automatically put arcsin⁡\arcsinarcsin around the right side and claim it equals A±BA\pm BA±B. The sum may be outside [−π/2,π/2][-\pi/2,\pi/2][−π/2,π/2].

For A=arccos⁡uA=\arccos uA=arccosu, B=arccos⁡vB=\arccos vB=arccosv,

cos⁡(A+B)=uv−1−u21−v2.\cos(A+B)=uv-\sqrt{1-u^2}\sqrt{1-v^2}.cos(A+B)=uv−1−u2​1−v2​.

Again,arccos⁡(cos⁡(A+B))=A+B\arccos(\cos(A+B))=A+Barccos(cos(A+B))=A+B requires A+B∈[0,π]A+B\in[0,\pi]A+B∈[0,π].

For acute angles: a sum is in (0,π)(0,\pi)(0,π) and a difference in (−π/2,π/2)(-\pi/2,\pi/2)(−π/2,π/2). These simple interval facts make many source problems safe.

Recognition: a domain may be so restrictive that no heavy trigonometry remains. Q11 has only two possible inputs before the angle equation is even solved.

Concept C08 — Range and an attained sum bound

First find the common domain,not the domain of just one summand.

For

f(x)=arcsin⁡x+arccos⁡x+arctan⁡x,f(x)=\arcsin x+\arccos x+\arctan x,f(x)=arcsinx+arccosx+arctanx,

the common domain is [−1,1][-1,1][−1,1]. The complementary pair is constant:

f(x)=π2+arctan⁡x.f(x)=\frac\pi2+\arctan x.f(x)=2π​+arctanx.

Arctangent increases from −π/4-\pi/4−π/4 to π/4\pi/4π/4 on this closed interval,so

range⁡(f)=[π/4,3π/4].\boxed{\operatorname{range}(f)=[\pi/4,3\pi/4]}.range(f)=[π/4,3π/4]​.

A maximum-sum pattern — important for JEE Main: if each ai≤Mia_i\le M_iai​≤Mi​ and ∑ai=∑Mi\sum a_i=\sum M_i∑ai​=∑Mi​,every individual term must reach its own upper bound. Otherwise a shortfall cannot be repaired by another term exceeding its bound.

Thus

arcsin⁡x+arcsin⁡y+arcsin⁡z=3π/2\arcsin x+\arcsin y+\arcsin z=3\pi/2arcsinx+arcsiny+arcsinz=3π/2

forces all three inverse sines to be π/2\pi/2π/2,so x=y=z=1x=y=z=1x=y=z=1.

Concept C09 — Domains: work from the outside inward

For real-valued expressions,

arcsin⁡g(x),arccos⁡g(x):−1≤g(x)≤1,\arcsin g(x),\arccos g(x):\quad -1\le g(x)\le1,arcsing(x),arccosg(x):−1≤g(x)≤1, arcsec⁡g(x),arccsc⁡g(x):∣g(x)∣≥1.\operatorname{arcsec}g(x),\operatorname{arccsc}g(x): \quad |g(x)|\ge1.arcsecg(x),arccscg(x):∣g(x)∣≥1.

Arctangent and inverse cotangent accept every real defined input. A denominator or square root inside still has its own restriction:

a(x)b(x): b(x)≠0,h(x): h(x)≥0.\frac{a(x)}{b(x)}:\ b(x)\ne0,\qquad \sqrt{h(x)}:\ h(x)\ge0.b(x)a(x)​: b(x)=0,h(x)​: h(x)≥0.

For a sum,all conditions hold together: use their intersection.

For arccos⁡(2x/(1+x))\arccos(2x/(1+x))arccos(2x/(1+x)),do not multiply an inequality by 1+x1+x1+x without knowing its sign. Move everything to one side and use a sign chart with its zero and pole.

For a quadratic input,combine two polynomial inequalities. In Q14,

−1≤x2−5x+5≤1-1\le x^2-5x+5\le1−1≤x2−5x+5≤1

leads to two disjoint intervals,not one:

[1,2]∪[3,4].\boxed{[1,2]\cup[3,4]}.[1,2]∪[3,4]​.

Concept C10 — Inverse-angle telescoping

For positive integer nnn,

tan⁡(arctan⁡(n+1)−arctan⁡n)=11+n(n+1).\tan\left(\arctan(n+1)-\arctan n\right) =\frac1{1+n(n+1)}.tan(arctan(n+1)−arctann)=1+n(n+1)1​.

The difference is positive and less than π/2\pi/2π/2,so

arccot⁡(1+n(n+1))=arctan⁡(n+1)−arctan⁡n.\boxed{\operatorname{arccot}(1+n(n+1)) =\arctan(n+1)-\arctan n}.arccot(1+n(n+1))=arctan(n+1)−arctann​.

Did you notice the pattern n(n+1)+1n(n+1)+1n(n+1)+1? It is the denominator produced by subtracting the tangents n+1n+1n+1 and nnn.

Adding adjacent differences cancels all middle angles:

∑n=1Narccot⁡(1+n(n+1))=arctan⁡(N+1)−arctan⁡1.\sum_{n=1}^{N}\operatorname{arccot}(1+n(n+1)) =\arctan(N+1)-\arctan1.n=1∑N​arccot(1+n(n+1))=arctan(N+1)−arctan1.

The sum lies in (0,π/4)(0,\pi/4)(0,π/4); its tangent is N/(N+2)N/(N+2)N/(N+2). Therefore

Ncot⁡(∑n=1Narccot⁡(1+n(n+1)))=N+2.\boxed{N\cot\left(\sum_{n=1}^{N}\operatorname{arccot}(1+n(n+1))\right)=N+2}.Ncot(n=1∑N​arccot(1+n(n+1)))=N+2​.

This shortcut uses the stated positive-integer pattern. A changed sign or different quadratic denominator needs a fresh branch check.

Concept C11 — Half angles and radical patterns

Let θ=arcsin⁡u\theta=\arcsin uθ=arcsinu with 0<u≤10<u\le10<u≤1. It is acute or right,and

tan⁡(θ/2)=sin⁡θ1+cos⁡θ=u1+1−u2.\boxed{\tan(\theta/2) =\frac{\sin\theta}{1+\cos\theta} =\frac{u}{1+\sqrt{1-u^2}}}.tan(θ/2)=1+cosθsinθ​=1+1−u2​u​​.

This form avoids subtracting nearly equal positive numbers. The rationalized form (1−1−u2)/u(1-\sqrt{1-u^2})/u(1−1−u2​)/u gives the same result. At u=0u=0u=0,use the first form to get zero.

For a different useful pattern,let θ=arctan⁡x\theta=\arctan xθ=arctanx. Then cos⁡θ>0\cos\theta>0cosθ>0 and 1+x2=sec⁡θ\sqrt{1+x^2}=\sec\theta1+x2​=secθ. For x≠0x\ne0x=0,

1+x2−1x=x1+x2+1=tan⁡(θ/2).\frac{\sqrt{1+x^2}-1}{x} =\frac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^2}+1} =\tan(\theta/2).x1+x2​−1​=1+x2​+1x​=tan(θ/2).

Since θ/2∈(−π/4,π/4)\theta/2\in(-\pi/4,\pi/4)θ/2∈(−π/4,π/4),

arctan⁡1+x2−1x=12arctan⁡x(x≠0).\boxed{\arctan\frac{\sqrt{1+x^2}-1}{x} =\frac12\arctan x\quad(x\ne0)}.arctanx1+x2​−1​=21​arctanx(x=0)​.

The right side exists at zero,but the original left fraction does not. A removable extension must be labelled separately.

Double-angle caution: arctan⁡(2x/(1−x2))=2arctan⁡x\arctan(2x/(1-x^2))=2\arctan xarctan(2x/(1−x2))=2arctanx holds for ∣x∣<1|x|<1∣x∣<1. For ∣x∣>1|x|>1∣x∣>1,the doubled angle leaves arctangent's principal range,and a π\piπ correction is needed. At x=±1x=\pm1x=±1,the displayed fraction is undefined.

Concept C12 — An angle difference can fix a quadratic expression

Let A=arccos⁡xA=\arccos xA=arccosx, B=arccos⁡zB=\arccos zB=arccosz,and A−B=δA-B=\deltaA−B=δ. Then

x=zcos⁡δ−sin⁡Bsin⁡δ.x=z\cos\delta-\sin B\sin\delta.x=zcosδ−sinBsinδ.

Hence

(x−zcos⁡δ)2=(1−z2)sin⁡2δ,(x-z\cos\delta)^2=(1-z^2)\sin^2\delta,(x−zcosδ)2=(1−z2)sin2δ,

which rearranges to

x2+z2−2xzcos⁡δ=sin⁡2δ.\boxed{x^2+z^2-2xz\cos\delta=\sin^2\delta}.x2+z2−2xzcosδ=sin2δ​.

Recognition: an inverse-cosine difference plus a quadratic target suggests this identity. It can remove both angles without finding either separately.

For Q19,z=y/2z=y/2z=y/2 and δ=π/3\delta=\pi/3δ=π/3. Multiplying the identity by 4 gives 4x2−2xy+y2=34x^2-2xy+y^2=34x2−2xy+y2=3.

The quadratic relation is a consequence of the original angle equation. It may include extra points if used as a reverse description: principal angle restrictions and signs still matter.

Concept C13 — Useful connection to Calculus

These derivative formulas belong to the Calculus chapters,but the principal branches explain their signs:

ddxarcsin⁡x=11−x2,ddxarccos⁡x=−11−x2(∣x∣<1),\frac{d}{dx}\arcsin x=\frac1{\sqrt{1-x^2}},\qquad \frac{d}{dx}\arccos x=-\frac1{\sqrt{1-x^2}} \quad(|x|<1),dxd​arcsinx=1−x2​1​,dxd​arccosx=−1−x2​1​(∣x∣<1), ddxarctan⁡x=11+x2,ddxarccot⁡x=−11+x2,\frac{d}{dx}\arctan x=\frac1{1+x^2},\qquad \frac{d}{dx}\operatorname{arccot}x=-\frac1{1+x^2},dxd​arctanx=1+x21​,dxd​arccotx=−1+x21​, ddxarcsec⁡x=1∣x∣x2−1,ddxarccsc⁡x=−1∣x∣x2−1(∣x∣>1).\frac{d}{dx}\operatorname{arcsec}x =\frac1{|x|\sqrt{x^2-1}},\qquad \frac{d}{dx}\operatorname{arccsc}x =-\frac1{|x|\sqrt{x^2-1}} \quad(|x|>1).dxd​arcsecx=∣x∣x2−1​1​,dxd​arccscx=−∣x∣x2−1​1​(∣x∣>1).

For a composite input u(x)u(x)u(x),multiply by u′(x)u'(x)u′(x) and check the strict derivative-domain conditions. An included endpoint in a function's domain need not have a finite derivative.

The absolute value in inverse-secant/cosecant derivatives is important on negative inputs. Do not replace it by xxx.

so arccos⁡(cos⁡10)=4π−10\arccos(\cos10)=4\pi-10arccos(cos10)=4π−10.

Question 5 — A sum at the upper bound forces every term to its bound

PDF page 135 | Numerical value | Notes: C02,C08

If sin⁡−1x+sin⁡−1y+sin⁡−1z=3π2\sin^{-1}x+\sin^{-1}y+\sin^{-1}z=\frac{3\pi}{2}sin−1x+sin−1y+sin−1z=23π​,then x+2y+3zx+2y+3zx+2y+3z equals ____.

Three such angles can add to 3π/23\pi/23π/2 only if all three reach π/2\pi/2π/2. If one were smaller,the others could not exceed their own caps to make up the difference.

arcsin⁡x=arcsin⁡y=arcsin⁡z=π/2⟹x=y=z=1.\arcsin x=\arcsin y=\arcsin z=\pi/2 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad x=y=z=1.arcsinx=arcsiny=arcsinz=π/2⟹x=y=z=1. x+2y+3z=1+2+3=6.\boxed{x+2y+3z=1+2+3=6}.x+2y+3z=1+2+3=6​.

A compact algebraic view: the three nonnegative deficits π/2−arcsin⁡x\pi/2-\arcsin xπ/2−arcsinx, π/2−arcsin⁡y\pi/2-\arcsin yπ/2−arcsiny, π/2−arcsin⁡z\pi/2-\arcsin zπ/2−arcsinz sum to zero. Each deficit must be zero.

2x1+x≤1  ⟺  x−1x+1≤0  ⟺  −1<x≤1.\frac{2x}{1+x}\le1 \iff\frac{x-1}{x+1}\le0 \iff -1<x\le1.1+x2x​≤1⟺x+1x−1​≤0⟺−1<x≤1.

2x1+x≥−1  ⟺  3x+1x+1≥0  ⟺  x<−1 or x≥−13.\frac{2x}{1+x}\ge-1 \iff\frac{3x+1}{x+1}\ge0 \iff x<-1\ \text{or}\ x\ge-\frac13.1+x2x​≥−1⟺x+13x+1​≥0⟺x<−1 or x≥−31​.

Intersect both results:

[−13,1];(b).\boxed{\left[-\frac13,1\right];\quad\text{(b)}}.[−31​,1];(b)​.

[π4,3π4];(b).\boxed{\left[\frac\pi4,\frac{3\pi}4\right];\quad\text{(b)}}.[4π​,43π​];(b)​.

Question 8 — Adjacent arctangent differences make a telescoping angle sum

PDF page 135 | Numerical value | Notes: C06,C10

After this chapter

An inverse expression returns an angle in a specified interval. Keep the domain beside its input and the principal range beside its output. Triangle identities do the arithmetic; branch checks make the answer valid. Every alternative remains visible for the later booklet. The supplied questions are practice,not verified actual PYQs.
